It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook. We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. => Évaluer au-delà du résultat final : détecter les échecs intermédiaires, la propagation d'erreurs et les dérives de comportement le long de la trajectoire => Concevoir et éprouver des workflows agentiques : décomposition de tâches, enchaînement d'agents (planner / executor / critic), points de contrôle et garde-fous => Construire des jeux de tests et scénarios de simulation d'utilisateurs : jobs.jd: The Role Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. Building agents is no longer the bottleneck. Improving them is: knowing whether a change made the agent better, why a conversation failed, and which part of the system should be fixed. You'll build the loop that makes our agents improve themselves — finding failures in real use, deciding which part of the agent harness is responsible, checking every proposed fix on cases the fixer never saw, and turning each fixed failure into a permanent test. We improve the system around the model: instructions, tool descriptions, routing, knowledge and memory. We don't train the model itself. The work is blend of ML and systems engineering. You'll decide whether a signal is trustworthy enough to act on, and build the infrastructure that produces that signal reproducibly across hundreds of customer organizations. This isn't a model-training role, and it isn't a testing role. It's applied ML at a point where the methodology genuinely isn't settled: LLMs judging LLMs is an open research problem, and we're working it against agents that take real, irreversible actions in stateful, multi-tenant enterprise environments. What you get to do in this role: Judge design and calibration A shared base judge with per-item rubrics expressed as configuration next to the dataset — so eval authors express intent, rather than forking a prompt per eval Splitting the problem correctly: deterministic validators for checkable world state ("was the ticket created, with the right item, routed to the right approver?"), and an LLM judge for the parts that are genuinely fuzzy — was the clarifying question appropriate, was policy followed, was the path efficient Scoring that reports its own confidence , so uncertain judgements route to a human instead of quietly becoming trusted signal A standing calibration loop against human-labeled trajectories, run in partnership with our annotation team — they own the human labeling, you own the calibrated judge artifact. How consistently humans agree with each other sets the ceiling on how good any judge can be, so raising that ceiling is part of the job Guarding against correlated blind spots: our user simulator and our judge are both LLMs, and they can be wrong in the same direction Offline↔online divergence: when simulation and production disagree, being the person who can say why, and keeping the suite re-seeded from new production failures so it can't quietly overfit Self-improving agent harness This is where the pillar is headed, and a large part of why the seat exists. You'll build the components that let the agent harness get better from its own use, without changing the model underneath. Finding what to improve: surfacing where the agent falls short in real use, including failures that look like success Synthetic data and environments: generating scenarios and the seeded enterprise worlds they run in — with expected outcomes and checks — from real failures or ahead of what customers ask for, and making sure what gets generated is realistic, hard enough, and doesn't leak the answer Deciding where a fix belongs: understanding why the agent failed and which part of the harness should change: its instructions, tools, routing, knowledge or memory Proposing improvements: optimizing those components against simulation rather than against production traffic Checking before anything ships: verifying every proposed change on cases it wasn't tuned on, catching regressions an average would hide, and keeping the part that proposes a change separate from the part that judges it Evals that grow: every fixed failure becomes a permanent test, so the suite gets stronger the more the agent is used Safe across many customers: learnings stay scoped to one organization where they must, and admins approve anything org-specific The infrastructure that runs it: a loop that runs reproducibly, at scale, across hundreds of customer organizations The guardrail that keeps it honest: end-state outcomes are what we hold the agent to To be successful in this role you have: 2+ years in applied ML, data science, or ML-adjacent engineering, with a track record of work that shipped and got used Experience turning subjective human judgement into a measurement that holds up — one that other people, and ideally other models, can act on. This is the core of the job Strong applied ML fundamentals, and comfort treating LLMs as a component you evaluate, prompt, and fine-tune rather than one you pretrain Strong Python, and the discipline to ship production-grade code rather than notebooks Ability to think and communicate clearly about complex problems — a large part of this job is convincing engineers that a number means what you say it means, and being right A high degree of ownership and a bias toward shipping at startup pace Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgement to know when a measurement is good enough to act on Experience in at least 3 of these: LLM-as-judge or automated evaluation design, and calibrating it against human judgement Human annotation programs: rubric authoring, label quality, and annotator throughput as a real constraint Search ranking, recsys, or online experimentation evaluation — golden-set staleness, offline/online divergence, side-by-side rater agreement. jobs.jd:
PolyAI is the Agentic Dialog Platform for building the conversational enterprise, used to build, run, govern, and improve dialog agents at scale. Powered by Raven, a proprietary dialog model trained on more than a billion enterprise conversations, PolyAI agents are built for complexity, open at every layer, and sovereign by design. PolyAI serves hundreds of enterprises across 75 languages and 25 countries, including Metro Bank, Marriott, PG&E, and UniCredit.

The role

Most AI agents are demos. Ours answer the phone for some of the biggest brands in the world: more than 100 million calls a year, across 2,000+ live deployments. Someone is on the line trying to move a booking, report a fault or pay a bill, and the agent either works or it doesn't.

We looking for a Forward Deployment Engineer who has built and shipped LLM agents in production, including tool use and evals. Forward Deployed Engineers are the people who make it work. You own a customer's agents from the first scoping call through to production and beyond. You design how the agent behaves, write the code that connects it to the customer's systems, put it on their phone lines, measure it and keep making it better.

This is not sales engineering and it is not support. You ship code that runs in production, and you own what happens after it ships.

We want someone who already builds agents because they can't help it, and who wants to do it at the hard end: real-time voice, messy enterprise systems, and callers who notice every mistake.

What you'll do

  • Own agents in production, end to end. Scope with the customer; design the conversation, the tools and the guardrails; build in Agent Studio and our ADK; launch; and stay accountable for how it performs.
  • You have built and shipped LLM agents in production, including tool use and evals 
  • Connect agents to the real world. Integrate CRMs, booking engines, payment flows and twenty-year-old APIs in Python. Work across SIP, telephony and contact-centre platforms. Make tool calls fast and reliable in the middle of a live conversation.
  • Debug live calls. When a call goes wrong, work out whether it was the speech recognition, the model, the prompt, an integration or the phone line, and fix the right thing.
  • Run agents like a scientist. Build eval sets from real calls, run A/B tests and let data decide what ships. Containment, resolution and caller experience are your numbers.
  • Close the gap to the platform. When you solve something for one customer, turn it into a reusable tool, template or product change so the next deployment is faster.   • Work AI-native. You use coding agents and LLM tooling every day, and you help the people around you do the same.

jobs.jd: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior. This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows. Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work. In this role, you will: Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software. Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption. Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability. Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform. Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value. Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved. Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools. Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development.
